chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Zarif ibn Nasih, from Abu Maryam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

If a man fasts something from the month of Ramadan and remains ill until he dies, there is nothing upon him [to make up]. And if he recovered, then became ill again, then died, and he had wealth, charity is given on his behalf; and if he did not have wealth, his heir gives charity on his behalf.

key_terms.تُصَدِّقَ عَنْهُ: Charity is given on his behalf

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a person who dies in Ramadan without fasting?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Isfahani distinguishes between continuous and intermittent illness to determine the obligation of *fidya* (compensation) for missed fasts, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that liability attaches only when the individual had the capacity to fast. The hadith clarifies that continuous illness exempts one entirely, while recovery followed by death triggers a financial obligation on the estate or heirs, ensuring the spiritual debt is settled. This nuance highlights the practical application of divine mercy in cases where death interrupts the fulfillment of obligatory acts.
